Get Combinations

Source: R/wildcard.R
get_combinations.Rd

Lists the theme / sub_theme / topic / geography_type / geography / metric combinations that match a query, without downloading any data. Use it to explore what is available, or to check how many datasets a wildcard query in get_data would download.

Usage

get_combinations(
  theme = "*",
  sub_theme = NULL,
  topic = NULL,
  geography_type = NULL,
  geography = NULL,
  metric = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

theme

the largest overall topical subgroup of data. For example infectious_disease.

sub_theme

a topical subgroup associated with the parent theme. For example respiratory.

topic

categorical subgroup associated with the selected theme and sub_theme. For example, COVID-19.

geography_type

the overarching area type for the intended geography. For example Nation.

geography

the selected area under the geography_type. For example England.

metric

the type of data being selected. For example COVID-19_testing_PCRcountByDay.

verbose

show progress messages.

Value

           data.frame with one row per matching combination,
                   or \code{NULL} (invisibly) if the query could not be
                   resolved, in which case the available options are
                   shown as a message.

Details

Each argument accepts a single value, a character vector of values, "*" for every available value, or a glob pattern containing * or ? (for example "NHS*London*").

Resolution stops at the last argument supplied, so get_combinations(theme = "*", sub_theme = "*") lists every sub-theme of every theme without looking further down the hierarchy.

Examples

# \donttest{
# every topic in every sub-theme of infectious_disease
get_combinations(theme = "infectious_disease", sub_theme = "*", topic = "*")

get_combinations(
  theme = "infectious_disease",
  sub_theme = "antimicrobial_resistance",
  topic = "E-coli",
  geography_type = "Integrated Care Board",
  geography = "*",
  metric = "*PercentResistant*"
)
